text:
nora: hey everyone, first-day snag. i'm on Fedora and trying to run `docker-compose up` for the repo. postgres container fails with `initdb: could not change permissions of directory "/var/lib/postgresql/data": Permission denied`. i'm using a host bind `./pgdata:/var/lib/postgresql/data`. SELinux is enabled. any Fedora/SELinux tips?

miguel: welcome :wave: sounds like SELinux is the culprit. Two quick approaches: 1) use the `:Z` mount option in compose to relabel the host dir for containers (e.g. `./pgdata:/var/lib/postgresql/data:Z`) or 2) change the SELinux label manually: `sudo chcon -Rt svirt_sandbox_file_t ./pgdata`. Named docker volumes also avoid SELinux bind-mount headaches.

sam: +1. Also ensure perms/owner are okay: Postgres expects strict perms, so `chmod 700 ./pgdata` and either `sudo chown -R 999:999 ./pgdata` or run the helper: `docker run --rm -v "$(pwd)/pgdata":/data alpine sh -c "chown -R 999:999 /data"`. Note: changing ownership won't fix SELinux context by itself.

nora: tried adding `:Z` to the compose bind but still saw permission denied in the container logs. `ls -Z ./pgdata` shows unconfined_u:object_r:user_home_t:s0.

miguel: if `:Z` didn't relabel, engine might not have applied it to existing files. Try the manual relabel: `sudo chcon -Rt svirt_sandbox_file_t ./pgdata`. After that `ls -Z ./pgdata` should show svirt_sandbox_file_t context. If you're debugging quickly, you can `sudo setenforce 0` to switch SELinux to permissive (NOT recommended long-term).

sam: one more gotcha: if the directory was created by root in a prior run, or by a different UID mapping, you might need to `docker-compose down`, remove the dir contents and re-create the dir, then chcon/chown before `up`. Also prefer named volumes in dev on SELinux hosts: in compose define `volumes: pgdata:` and `- pgdata:/var/lib/postgresql/data` so Docker manages labels.

nora: ran `sudo chcon -Rt svirt_sandbox_file_t ./pgdata` + `chmod 700 ./pgdata` and then `docker-compose up` again. Postgres init finished and migrations ran. woohoo :tada: thanks both!

infra-bot: onboarding note: for Linux hosts with SELinux, we recommend using named volumes or the `:Z` mount option. If bind mounts are required, `chcon -Rt svirt_sandbox_file_t` will usually fix permission denials. See internal docs: https://intranet.redwood.dev/dev-setup#selinux-local-db

nora: saving this thread in my notes. appreciate the quick help :slightly_smiling_face:
